marks.gloss_en: the matron: what can I do to you, since you do not wipe with a shard, do not kill lice on your garments, and do not pull a vegetable and eat it from the bundle the gardener tied
אף על פי שאין ראיה לדבר זכר לדבר: לא ימצא במכתתו חרש לחתות אש מיקוד -- a shard to scoop fire is named as a thing of worth
אמר לו רבי יוסי: משם ראיה? ולחשוף מים מגבא -- is there proof from there? [the verse goes on:] 'and to draw water from a cistern'
R' Meir: [the measure for a shard is] enough to scoop fire with
אף על פי שאין ראיה לדבר, זכר לדבר -- Isa 30:14: a shard to take fire from the hearth (graded by R' Meir himself as allusion, not proof)
אמר לו רבי יוסי: משם ראיה? ולחשוף מים מגבא -- the same verse goes on to a shard for scooping water, so it shows nothing for R' Meir's measure
R' Meir reads the verse as 'no need to say': no need to say that a thing significant to people shall not be found -- even a thing insignificant to people shall not be found
אמר אביי: [מתניתין נמי] לחתות אש מיקידה גדולה -- the mishna's fire-raking shard is for a large blaze, so R' Meir's measure is the larger in the mishna too
by reasoning, R' Yosei's measure (a shard holding a revi'it) is the larger
תזרם כמו דוה -- מה נדה מטמאה במשא, אף עבודה זרה מטמאה במשא (repeated in the AZ mishna at 82b.1)
idolatry is juxtaposed in Scripture to a nidda ('cast them away as a menstruant', Isa 30:22)
one whose house adjoined an idol's house and fell may not rebuild it; he moves four amot into his own land and builds
תניא כמאן דאמר רוח זוהמא שולטת בו -- the baraita calls eating while needing to relieve oneself 'the beginning of the spirit of filth'
one said: one who needs to relieve himself and does not -- an evil spirit takes hold of him
מיתיבי: המקנח בדבר שהאור שולטת בו שיניו התחתונות נושרות -- grasses are such a thing, so how may he wipe with them?
לא קשיא: הא בלחין, הא ביבשין -- the view permitting grasses speaks of moist ones, the baraita of dry ones
one said: if a stone and grasses are before him, he wipes with the stone and does not wipe with the grasses
אמר ליה רב אחא בריה דרבא לרב אשי: כל שכן דכי מסח דעתיה לא מפני! -- all the more so, if he diverts his mind he will not relieve himself
אמר ליה: יסיח דעתו מדברים אחרים -- divert his mind FROM other matters (= p_ashi_midvarim_acherim)
Rav Chisda: one who needs to relieve himself and cannot should stand and sit, stand and sit
the baraita: one who enters a fixed meal walks, relieves himself, and enters and sits in his place
הוא עסיק בחיי דברייתא ואת אמרת במילי דעלמא?! -- he deals with the life of creatures, and you call it worldly matters?!
Rav Huna: Rav Chisda's teachings are sharp
תרגמה רפרם בר פפא קמיה דרב חסדא אליבא דרב הונא: באוגני כלים -- the baraita's 'shard' is the rim of a vessel (= p_rafram_ognei_kelim)
Rav Huna: if a stone and a shard are before him, he wipes with the stone and does not wipe with the shard
